name: exp2b_subsets_stageB
algorithm: exhaustive enumeration of structurally feasible geometry edit subsets; frequency re-optimized per subset inside one pinned envelope; every plan scored by the frozen Model B evaluator

config_snapshot.assumptions.yaml:
# Model assumptions. Everything here is an explicit research assumption,
# not a verified COTA operating parameter.
crs:
  geographic: "EPSG:4326"
  projected: "EPSG:32617"   # UTM 17N, meters — used for all planar distance math

service_periods:
  # Weekday periods, local time, [start_hour, end_hour). Trips assigned by first
  # departure time. GTFS times >24:00 fold into 'owl'.
  early:   [4, 6]
  am_peak: [6, 9]
  midday:  [9, 15]
  pm_peak: [15, 18]
  evening: [18, 22]
  owl:     [22, 28]

operations:
  # Layover/recovery as fraction of round-trip running time (industry-typical
  # 10–20%; NOT a verified COTA work rule). NTD cannot pin this down: annual
  # scheduled hours come in 9.2% BELOW reported VRH while scheduled miles come
  # in 13.7% ABOVE reported VRM, so the hours gap cannot be attributed to
  # layover alone (the 2024 report year vs the May-2026 feed is the other
  # candidate — COTA's VRH grew 13.3% from 2023 to 2024).
  layover_ratio: 0.15
  # Deadhead, operator availability: UNKNOWN — not modeled.
  min_terminal_layover_min: 3
  # NTD 2024 reported facts (agency 50016, motorbus, directly operated).
  # Recorded for reporting and constraint sanity checks; not model inputs.
  ntd_voms: 198                    # vehicles operated in maximum service
  ntd_vams: 285                    # vehicles available for maximum service
  ntd_spare_ratio_pct: 43.9        # was classified ESTIMABLE; now known
  ntd_avg_fleet_age_years: 6.5
  ntd_opex_per_revenue_hour: 209.68

demand_proxy:
  # Stop catchment radius for allocating block-group jobs/residents to stops (m).
  catchment_radius_m: 600
  # Trip generation weights: how strongly residents vs jobs near a stop drive
  # boardings. Proxy values; calibrate against APC when available.
  resident_weight: 1.0
  job_weight: 1.0
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # SCALE — now NTD-anchored, no longer a guess.
  # The proxy's raw units are "workers + jobs allocated to stops within the
  # catchment" (~940k for Central Ohio) — a relative measure, not trips.
  # Unscaled it models every bus at ~400 passengers and lets the crowding term
  # dominate the objective, so it is rescaled to a weekday linked-trip total.
  # Derived from NTD 2024 (agency 50016): average weekday UPT 38,694 x bus
  # share of annual UPT 95.98% = 37,139 weekday bus boardings; divided by
  # (1 + transfer_rate 0.20) = 30,949 linked trips. Sensitivity is still swept.
  assumed_weekday_linked_trips: 30949
  # Temporal distribution of weekday transit demand by period (fractions sum to 1).
  # Shaped from typical US bus demand profiles; NOT COTA-observed.
  period_shares:
    early: 0.05
    am_peak: 0.22
    midday: 0.33
    pm_peak: 0.24
    evening: 0.12
    owl: 0.04

waiting:
  # Expected wait as a function of headway h (minutes).
  # If h <= random_arrival_threshold: E[wait] = h/2 (random arrivals).
  # Else: E[wait] = threshold/2 + schedule_coefficient * (h - threshold)
  # (passengers consult schedules on infrequent service).
  random_arrival_threshold_min: 12
  schedule_coefficient: 0.25
  # Demand retention vs headway: fraction of proxy demand actually served falls
  # linearly from 1.0 at headway<=retention_full_min to retention_floor at
  # headway>=retention_zero_min. Beyond policy_max_headway all demand unserved.
  retention_full_min: 15
  retention_zero_min: 120
  retention_floor: 0.25

passenger:
  # Mean share of a route's one-way runtime that an average passenger rides.
  # DERIVED from NTD 2024: bus passenger-miles / unlinked trips = 4.601 mi per
  # boarding; mean one-way route runtime 64.8 min at the NTD in-service speed of
  # 12.20 mph = 13.18 mi end to end; 4.601 / 13.18 = 0.349. This independently
  # confirms the 0.35 originally assumed, to within 0.2%.
  avg_ride_fraction: 0.349
  # Mean access walk time per trip (each end), minutes. Assumption.
  access_walk_min: 5.0
  # Share of passenger trips involving one transfer. COTA's observed rate is
  # UNKNOWN (would come from APC/fare data); 0.20 is a typical mid-size bus value.
  transfer_rate: 0.20

# Path-based (RAPTOR) assignment. Used by Experiment 2.
path_assignment:
  # Waiting-time model for a ride leg.
  #   "pattern"    Model A: the chosen pattern's own headway. Correct when that
  #                pattern is the only one that can carry the movement.
  #   "same_route" Model B: the combined frequency of every same-route pattern
  #                that serves the boarding stop, the alighting stop, and in
  #                that order. A passenger boards whichever arrives first.
  # Model A undervalues high-frequency trunk service, which runs the most
  # pattern variants, so it is biased against exactly the routes the frequency
  # optimizer proposes to cut. Measured at ~4.3% of generalized cost.
  # This stays "pattern" so Model A remains reproducible as the control.
  # It is therefore a trap for any caller that builds an evaluator without
  # passing common_lines explicitly: it will get Model A no matter what the
  # run is labelled. That happened -- see the defect note in ACCEPTANCE.md,
  # 2026-08-27 to 2026-08-29. build_setup now logs a WARNING whenever this
  # default is what supplied the value.
  common_lines: pattern
  walk_radius_m: 400          # stop-to-stop footpath radius for transfers
  walk_speed_m_per_min: 80    # 4.8 km/h
  access_radius_m: 600        # zone centroid to boarding stop
  max_rounds: 3               # boardings, i.e. up to 2 transfers
  max_paths_per_od: 4
  n_random_scenarios: 3       # extra frequency draws used to widen the path set
  od_top_k: 20000
  # Trip retention as a function of the WHOLE journey's generalized cost, not
  # just headway — this supersedes the headway-only retention curve used by the
  # route-level experiment, because a path-based model knows the full journey.
  # Linear from 1.0 at cost_retention_full to the floor at cost_retention_zero.
  # A crude discouragement proxy, NOT a mode-choice model (see Step 11).
  cost_retention_full_min: 60      # ~1 h perceived travel: nobody is put off
  cost_retention_zero_min: 210
  cost_retention_floor: 0.10

crowding:
  bus_capacity: 60          # seated+standing planning capacity per 40-ft bus
  # Crowding multiplier on in-vehicle time once load factor exceeds 1.0
  crowding_penalty_per_excess_load: 1.0
config_snapshot.cost_weights.yaml:
# Generalized passenger cost weights, in equivalent in-vehicle minutes.
# Values follow common transit planning practice (e.g., TCRP 165 ranges);
# they are assumptions, not COTA-calibrated.
weights:
  walking: 2.0            # per walk minute
  waiting: 2.0            # per expected wait minute
  in_vehicle: 1.0         # per in-vehicle minute
  transfer_wait: 2.0      # per transfer wait minute
  transfer_penalty: 10.0  # fixed minutes-equivalent per transfer
  crowding: 1.0           # extra multiplier applied via crowding model
  reliability: 0.0        # placeholder until empirical RT data exists
  unserved: 60.0          # minutes-equivalent penalty per unserved trip
config_snapshot.constraints.yaml:
# Service constraints for frequency optimization.
resource:
  # Budgets are set to "baseline" — computed from the current GTFS — unless
  # overridden with explicit numbers here.
  weekday_revenue_vehicle_hours: baseline
  peak_fleet_by_period: baseline
  # Solutions may not exceed the baseline envelope at all. Set to 0 so the claim
  # "inside COTA's current resource envelope" needs no asterisk.
  budget_tolerance: 0.0

service:
  policy_max_headway_min: 60      # no route-period may exceed this if it had service
  policy_min_headway_min: 5       # floor; below this bunching dominates
  headway_ladder_min: [5, 6, 7.5, 10, 12, 15, 20, 24, 30, 40, 45, 60]
  preserve_span: true             # a route-period with baseline service keeps service
  allow_new_service_in_empty_periods: false
config_snapshot.sources.yaml:
# Authoritative data sources for the COTA transit optimization project.
# status: AVAILABLE | BLOCKED_EGRESS (verified URL, sandbox cannot fetch; user-mediated
#         retrieval) | UNKNOWN (not yet located) | NOT_RETRIEVED
sources:
  cota_gtfs_static:
    name: COTA GTFS static feed
    publisher: Central Ohio Transit Authority
    url: https://www.cota.com/data/cota.gtfs.zip
    retrieval_date: null  # set by registry at ingest
    data_type: GTFS static (zip of CSV)
    coverage: COTA fixed-route network, current signup
    license: >-
      COTA data terms (cota.com/data): non-exclusive, limited, revocable right to
      use/reproduce/redistribute; as-is, no warranty; no COTA trademark use.
    download_method: HTTP GET (user-mediated in this environment)
    status: BLOCKED_EGRESS
    notes: URL confirmed on cota.com/data 2026-08-25.
  cota_gtfs_rt_alerts:
    name: COTA GTFS-Realtime service alerts
    publisher: COTA / Vontas
    url: https://gtfs-rt.cota.vontascloud.com/TMGTFSRealTimeWebService/Alert/Alerts.pb
    data_type: GTFS-RT protobuf
    coverage: live alerts
    license: same COTA data terms
    download_method: HTTP GET
    status: BLOCKED_EGRESS
    notes: Confirmed on cota.com/data 2026-08-25.
  cota_gtfs_rt_trip_updates:
    name: COTA GTFS-Realtime trip updates
    publisher: COTA via Swiftly
    url: https://api.goswift.ly/real-time/cota/gtfs-rt-trip-updates
    data_type: GTFS-RT protobuf
    coverage: live trip updates
    download_method: HTTP GET with public apiKey query param published on cota.com/data
    status: BLOCKED_EGRESS
    notes: Public key published by COTA on its data page; not stored here.
  cota_gtfs_rt_vehicle_positions:
    name: COTA GTFS-Realtime vehicle positions
    publisher: COTA via Swiftly
    url: https://api.goswift.ly/real-time/cota/gtfs-rt-vehicle-positions
    data_type: GTFS-RT protobuf
    coverage: live vehicle positions
    download_method: HTTP GET with public apiKey query param published on cota.com/data
    status: BLOCKED_EGRESS
  cota_gis_open_data:
    name: COTA open GIS data portal
    publisher: COTA
    url: http://cota1974.maps.arcgis.com/home/index.html
    data_type: ArcGIS Online items (shapefile/GeoJSON services)
    coverage: routes, stops, park & ride
    status: BLOCKED_EGRESS
    notes: Linked from cota.com/data.
  ntd_cota:
    name: National Transit Database 2024 Annual Agency Profile — COTA (NTD ID 50016)
    publisher: Federal Transit Administration
    url: https://www.transit.dot.gov/sites/fta.dot.gov/files/transit_agency_profile_doc/2024/50016.pdf
    data_type: annual agency statistics (VRM, VRH, fleet, ridership, opex)
    coverage: COTA, calendar year 2024
    license: US federal government work, public domain
    download_method: HTTP GET (user-mediated in this environment)
    status: BLOCKED_EGRESS
    notes: >-
      COTA's NTD ID is 50016 (an earlier guess of 50066 was wrong). Parsed
      deterministically by cota_opt.ntd, which rejects any parse that fails to
      reproduce the profile's own 18 printed efficiency ratios. Supplies the
      weekday-boardings anchor for the demand scale, the passenger trip length
      that validates avg_ride_fraction, VOMS/VAMS/spare ratio, and operating
      expense per revenue hour. Prior-year profiles use the same URL pattern.
  lodes_od_oh:
    name: LEHD LODES8 Ohio OD (JT00, main)
    publisher: US Census Bureau LEHD
    url: https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/lodes/LODES8/oh/od/oh_od_main_JT00_2022.csv.gz
    data_type: block-to-block home→work job flows
    coverage: Ohio, 2022
    status: BLOCKED_EGRESS
    notes: Large; WAC/RAC used first for stop-catchment weights.
  lodes_wac_oh:
    name: LEHD LODES8 Ohio WAC (S000 JT00 2022)
    publisher: US Census Bureau LEHD
    url: https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/lodes/LODES8/oh/wac/oh_wac_S000_JT00_2022.csv.gz
    data_type: jobs by workplace census block
    coverage: Ohio, 2022
    status: BLOCKED_EGRESS
  lodes_rac_oh:
    name: LEHD LODES8 Ohio RAC (S000 JT00 2022)
    publisher: US Census Bureau LEHD
    url: https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/lodes/LODES8/oh/rac/oh_rac_S000_JT00_2022.csv.gz
    data_type: workers by residence census block
    coverage: Ohio, 2022
    status: BLOCKED_EGRESS
  cenpop_bg_oh:
    name: 2020 Census block-group population centroids, Ohio
    publisher: US Census Bureau
    url: https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/reference/cenpop2020/blkgrp/CenPop2020_Mean_BG39.txt
    data_type: CSV (GEOID, population, mean center lat/lon)
    coverage: Ohio block groups
    status: BLOCKED_EGRESS
  acs_5yr:
    name: ACS 5-year estimates via Census API
    publisher: US Census Bureau
    url: https://api.census.gov/data/2023/acs/acs5
    data_type: demographic/commuting tables
    coverage: Franklin County + neighbors, tract/BG
    status: BLOCKED_EGRESS
    notes: >-
      Relevant variables — B01003_001E population; B08301 means of transportation
      to work (B08301_010E transit); B08201/B25044 vehicles available
      (zero-car households); B19013_001E median household income; B23025 employment
      status; S1810/B18101 disability. Recorded for future retrieval; no normative
      demographic weights are embedded in optimization.
  morpc_traffic_counts:
    name: MORPC regional traffic count database
    publisher: Mid-Ohio Regional Planning Commission
    url: UNKNOWN
    data_type: traffic counts
    status: UNKNOWN
    notes: Not yet located from within sandbox; MORPC hosts counts via its GIS portal.
  odot_traffic:
    name: ODOT Traffic Count/TDMS data
    publisher: Ohio DOT
    url: UNKNOWN
    data_type: statewide traffic monitoring
    status: UNKNOWN
  cota_planning_docs:
    name: COTA planning documents (LinkUS, System Redesign, APC/ridership reports)
    publisher: COTA
    url: UNKNOWN
    data_type: PDF reports
    status: UNKNOWN
    notes: Stop-level APC data likely requires a public records request.
